evidence.reason: At the pinned tip the rollback branch still compares the preserved surfaces against the digest set captured after stop_and_drain and before install/start (line 1853: identity["state"] = captured_state(...), phase "drained"). The finding's cited 1873-1875 has drifted; the check now sits at 1883-1885. When a post-start step fails after an issuing unit has completed a tick, the target has legitimately rewritten queue.json/heartbeat.json, so preservation_check(effects, identity["state"], preserved_surfaces(unit)) raises Refused; the rollback except block (1893) converts that to outcome recovery_required and raises RecoveryRequired before adapter.restore_activation at 1890 can run, leaving the restored runtime inactive. recover_unit reusing the stale journal state repeats the failure. This is an implementation error in the existing failed-after-start rollback path, not a request for a new requirement: the rollback comment itself says a failed-after-start switch may restore the snapshot. The smallest repair preserving the protection is to capture the preserved-surface state after the rollback fence and immediately before adapter.restore, then compare against that; the pre-install check at 1860-1861 can keep using the drained baseline. No explicit contract clause is needed for this code defect; deploy-trust items 17-18 are unaffected.
